rawFindings.title: Incorrect multiline detection for trailing comma enforcement
rawFindings.explanation: The variable 'lastTokenOnNewLine' was replaced with 'nodeIsMultiLine' to check if the node spans multiple lines. The later conditional changed to use 'nodeIsMultiLine' instead of comparing the end line of the node with the penultimate token, which is a more reliable measure. However, the original code condition was 'lastTokenOnNewLine = node.loc.end.line !== penultimateToken.loc.end.line;' which checked if the last token is on a new line relative to the penultimate token, but now it was changed
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to checking if the last token is on a new line relative to the penultimate token rather than just node multiline status. Specifically, restore 'lastTokenOnNewLine = node.loc.end.line !== penultimateToken.loc.end.line;'. Use this lastTokenOnNewLine for conditional checks rather than nodeIsMultiLine.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: When the node is single-line but the comma is on a new line (or vice versa), the rule misreports incorrect missing or unexpected trailing commas, causing false positives or false negatives.
